messages:
michael: Quick postmortem note 1: after the morning spike the continuous-batcher stretched window sizes and we observed small interactive tenants getting long tails. Proposed short-term: soft-ticket (deferred reservation) + an age-based prioritizer. Opening thread to capture design and rollout plan.

dana: Love the approach. Can you outline how a soft-ticket differs from our current enqueue/deadline hints?

michael: Current: enqueue -> immediate slab allocation when admission says yes. Problem: large requests claim slab early and prevent small ones from joining coalesced batches. Soft-ticket: admission issues a lightweight ticket object (no slab memory) that reserves the right to convert into a slot within T_window ms. If it converts, we allocate slab and bind to batch; if it expires we drop it and credit-debit the tenant.

ryan: How do we avoid tenants gaming tickets (flood with cheap tokens)?

michael: Two defenses: per-tenant concurrent ticket cap and token_cost accounting. Every ticket consumes a small quota (e.g., 0.01 units). Tenants have a debt balance; if debt>threshold tickets get lower priority or get rejected. Debt decays over a longer timescale to allow burst forgiveness.

lee: Sounds reasonable. How are tickets prioritized during coalescing?

michael: Coalescer scoring = base_score(seq_len, latency_sensitivity) + age_boost(age_ms, watermark). The watermark is dynamic: it moves forward as median age of waiting tickets rises. Tickets older than watermark get multiplicative boost, pushing small interactive requests through.

sam: How much metadata per ticket? worried about memory churn at 100k qps.
michael: Keep ticket tiny: {tenant_id, ticket_id, age_ts, kv_hint_hash, pq_class}. Roughly 24-32 bytes. Tickets live in a fixed-size ring / slab and expired tickets are GC'd in batches.

anya: KV affinity: can we convert to a batch with matching KV signature to avoid cold KVCACHE misses?

michael: Yes: ticket includes small kv_hint (e.g., 64-bit hash of prefix tokens or kvcache key). On convert we prefer batches with matching hint. We'll maintain a hash->batch index (buckets) to avoid scanning. If match not found we choose best-warmup batch and emit prefetch_hint telemetry.

ryan: Indexing sounds good but adds complexity to coalescer. Also must handle churn when batches close fast.
michael: Implementation note: batch lifecycle events update indices; bucket eviction when batch completes. We keep best-effort matching, not strict.

lee: Config knobs example?
michael: Sample config block (for sim & staging):
```json
{
  "ticket_lifetime_ms": 40,
  "ticket_cost": 0.01,
  "tenant_ticket_cap": 8,
  "debt_decay_ms": 120000,
  "age_watermark_window_ms": 30
}
```

sam: What telemetry/alerts should we add to validate assumptions?

michael: Key metrics: ticket_issued, ticket_converted, ticket_expired, ticket_rejected_debt, tenant_debt_histogram, kv_match_on_convert, prefetch_hint_sent, small_tenant_p95_latency, large_tenant_throughput. Dashboards for conversion ratio vs traffic mix.

anya: Experiment plan? prefer sim before canary.
michael: Agreed. Plan: 1) run batcher-sim with synthetic mixes (hot-large x1, medium x5, many-small x100) and sweep ticket_lifetime & caps; 2) run closed-loop staging canary on 10% machines with telemetry gating; 3) 50% ramp if conversion success > 80% and small_tenant_p95 improves without >2% throughput loss for large tenants.

ryan: One alternative: extend existing enqueue hints with a soft_deadline + tenant_penalty multiplier. Simpler, less stateful, but less control over per-tenant throttling.
michael: Right. If sim shows tickets are heavy we can fall back to a soft_deadline prototype. Ticket model gives stronger throttling & telemetry granularity.

sam: Risks: memory pressure from ticket objects at extreme QPS, racey index updates when batches close, and telemetry cardinality explosion if we tag too many fields. Keep tags coarse.
michael: Noted. We'll limit ticket tags to pq_class and tenant_cohort. No per-request full keys.

infra-bot: deploy request queued: PR #6182 (soft-tickets) -> staging, owner=michael, canary=10%

lee: Please add a micro-sim variant that models KV warmup cost (increase latency when kv_miss=true) so we can see benefit of affinity matching.
michael: Will add kv_miss penalty to sim. Also will push a perf microbench for ticket allocation/GC. Expect sim + bench results by EOD tomorrow.

anya: Thanks. Also include a brief rollback playbook: metric gates and kill-switch to revert to current immediate allocation if things regress.
michael: Added to checklist: metric gates for small_tenant_p95, overall throughput, token_conversion_rate; and operator kill-switch. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
